To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

cocaine and metabolites are detectable in saliva after intravenous, intramuscular, intranasal and smoking cocaine administration; the concentrations of cocaine are higher in saliva than plasma, and that saliva may be used for the detection of cocaine and its metabolites.
cocaine appears in saliva rapidly following intravenous, nasal, and smoked administration, and cocaine concentrations in saliva are generally higher than in plasma.
cocaine is rapidly absorbed from the oral mucosa, and saliva concentrations are generally greater than plasma cocaine concentrations following all routes of cocaine administration.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a rapid, simple, and inexpensive method for detecting the presence of cocaine in saliva.
the development of new and more sensitive methods for the analysis of drugs and drug metabolites in biological fluids.
the development and application of analytical techniques for the detection and quantitation of drugs of abuse and related compounds in body fluids.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

cocaine is detectable in saliva for 2 h after intravenous, 2.5 h after intranasal, or 1 h after smoked administration, and cocaine is detectable for 2.5, 3, and 3 h in plasma following intravenous, nasal, and smoked administration, respectively.
the cocaine concentrations in saliva are comparable to plasma concentrations, and the saliva is an appropriate matrix for the detection of cocaine and cocaine metabolites.

saliva can be a reliable matrix for the detection of cocaine, but the interpretation of saliva results must be done with caution, especially when the cocaine concentrations are high and/or the route of administration is intranasal or smoked.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cocaine and benzoylecogonine in saliva are not a reliable indicator of cocaine abuse.

the use of saliva for drug testing is a useful alternative to urine testing, and that saliva is a useful matrix for the detection of cocaine and its metabolites following all routes of drug administration.
saliva is an excellent matrix for the detection of cocaine and metabolites, and that the S/P ratios are generally greater than 0.9 for cocaine and metabolites.
The main takeaway from our work is that
saliva can be used for the detection and determination of cocaine and its metabolites following all routes of drug administration.
cocaine and its major metabolites are present in saliva after cocaine is administered by the three main routes.
saliva is a useful specimen for the detection of cocaine and its major metabolites.
